#| label: recompute

## Question and scope

Can the publication's processed TCGA breast cancer measurements and original
R implementation produce reproducible patient networks, clusters and survival
comparisons? This project reanalyzes the breast cohort in @wang2014 using
`r nrow(clinical)` patients with matched mRNA, DNA methylation, miRNA and
survival information.

This is a downstream reanalysis of the supplied normalized matrices. It does
not reconstruct raw TCGA preprocessing, and it does not recover the exact
published numerical result. The cohort uses the paper's microarray and HM27
measurements; it is not a substitution with modern RNA-seq or HM450 data.

## Inputs and checks

The publisher's supplementary data, software and methods are downloaded from
their recorded URLs, checked with SHA256, and made read-only. Only the breast
cohort and the original SNFtool source files required by the workflow are
extracted. `metadata/sources.json` and `metadata/inputs.sha256` identify the
exact resources. The software attachment reports SNFtool version
`r read.dcf(file.path(source_dir, "..", "DESCRIPTION"))[1, "Version"]`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-inputs
#| tbl-cap: "Input dimensions after patient matching; missing values are counted before analysis."
knitr::kable(qc[, c("view", "patients", "features", "missing")])
```

Patients are matched by the first twelve characters of the TCGA barcode and
ordered by the original clinical table. The parser handles doubled header
tabs and trailing row tabs without editing the input files. Duplicated IDs,
missing values, nonfinite measurements, inconsistent patients or unexpected
dimensions stop the run. No additional log transformation, imputation or
normalization is applied.

## Analysis choices

```{r}
#| label: tbl-settings
#| tbl-cap: "Primary settings recorded in config/analysis.json."
settings <- config[c("K", "alpha", "iterations", "clusters", "seed", "distance", "normalization")]
knitr::kable(data.frame(setting = names(settings), value = unlist(settings), row.names = NULL))
```

Euclidean distances produce one affinity network per data type. SNF fuses
these networks, and the original R spectral clustering function assigns the
same number of groups to each single network and the fused network. The
random number generator and seed are reset for each clustering. A standard
asymptotic log-rank test compares overall survival between groups; follow-up
is converted from days to months only for plotting. These choices were
retained from the original homework analysis rather than tuned to match the
publication's survival p-value.

## Networks, clusters and survival

![Individual affinity networks and the fused network. Every panel uses the SNF cluster ordering. Diagonals are zeroed for display only; each panel is scaled to its own off-diagonal 99th percentile, so absolute color intensity cannot be compared across panels.](../results/figure1_networks.png){#fig-networks fig-alt="Four patient by patient heatmaps for mRNA, methylation, miRNA and SNF, with boundaries marking the fused-network clusters."}

The fused-network cluster sizes are `r paste(sort(tabulate(labels$SNF, config$clusters)), collapse = ", ")`
(sorted to avoid assigning scientific meaning to cluster labels). There are
`r sum(clinical$Death)` observed deaths among `r nrow(clinical)` patients.
Ordering a network by its own clusters makes blocks easier to see; it is
not independent evidence that those groups are biologically valid.

![PCA of the centered fused matrix and Kaplan-Meier survival curves. This is analogous to the BIC panels of Supplementary Figure 15, using a two-dimensional projection rather than reconstructing the original coordinates or cluster assignments.](../results/figure2_embedding_survival.png){#fig-embedding fig-alt="A two-dimensional principal-component scatterplot colored by SNF cluster alongside survival curves with cluster sizes, censoring marks and the log-rank result."}

```{r}
#| label: tbl-survival
#| tbl-cap: "Computed log-rank p-values and the published BIC values transcribed from main Table 1."
comparison <- metrics[, c("method", "logrank_p", "paper_p", "cluster_sizes")]
names(comparison) <- c("Method", "This analysis: p", "Paper: p", "Cluster sizes (label order)")
knitr::kable(comparison, digits = 6)
```

The SNF log-rank p-value is `r fmt(snf_result$logrank_p)`, compared with
`r fmt(snf_result$paper_p)` in the publication. The method with the smallest
p-value in this run is `r metrics$method[which.min(metrics$logrank_p)]`.
This run does not reproduce the paper's numerical comparison, and a smaller
p-value alone is not a measure of clustering quality or clinical usefulness.

![Kaplan-Meier curves for all three single-omics clusterings and SNF. Curves omit confidence intervals and can be unstable late in follow-up, when few patients remain at risk.](../results/figure3_survival_comparison.png){#fig-survival fig-alt="Four survival panels comparing the five clusters from each individual measurement type and the fused network, each annotated with its log-rank p-value and group sizes."}

## Repeatability and sensitivity

The primary network and clustering are recomputed in the same R session with
the same inputs, parameters and random seed. Network differences are checked
numerically; partitions are compared through pairwise coassignment, which is
unchanged if cluster labels are permuted.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-repeatability
#| tbl-cap: "Within-run repeatability checks; the partition indicator must be one."
knitr::kable(data.frame(check = names(checks), value = unname(checks)))
```

The diagnostic grid is specified in the configuration and all combinations
are reported. It varies neighbors and iteration count, and contrasts
Euclidean distance with the squared-distance convention in the software's
README. No setting is selected by its survival result. Adjusted Rand index
(ARI) compares each diagnostic partition with the primary partition.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sensitivity
#| tbl-cap: "Complete prespecified sensitivity grid. ARI equals one for identical partitions, regardless of label numbering."
knitr::kable(diagnostics, digits = 6)
```

Repeatability under fixed settings does not imply robustness to changes of
settings, nor does it establish exact agreement with the original paper.

## Limitations and unresolved discrepancies

- The downloaded miRNA table has `r qc$features[qc$view == "miRNA"]`
  features, while Supplementary Table 1 lists
  `r config$paper$supplementary_table_miRNA_features` for BIC. The reason is
  unresolved; the workflow does not invent additional features.
- The paper describes Euclidean distance, but the bundled software example
  calls `dist2`, which returns squared Euclidean distances. The primary
  analysis and the diagnostic alternative are both identified explicitly.
- Exact BIC execution settings and original patient cluster assignments were
  not recovered from the inspected materials. The paper describes MATLAB
  experiments, while this project uses the supplied R implementation. The
  observed discrepancy cannot be assigned to one cause from this evidence.
- This complete-case cohort and its limited number of survival events do
  not establish representative, independently validated clinical subtypes.
- The validation command checks agreement with this project's reference
  analysis, not with the unavailable original clustering. Different
  platforms may differ in floating-point details; supported platforms must
  pass the numerical and partition checks rather than a bytewise PNG test.
